title: Working Papers
text:
with Hisahiro Naito
This paper examines whether the benefits of export-driven globalization are distributed evenly across regions. Using satellite-measured nighttime luminosity and a broad panel of developing countries, the study shows that trade integration generates stronger growth effects in urban trade hubs compared with surrounding rural areas. The findings highlight the importance of spatially inclusive trade policies that address uneven regional development.




with Hisahiro Naito
This study investigates how exchange rate uncertainty interacts with labor market rigidity to influence export performance. Using country–industry panel data, the paper jointly examines the effects of exchange rate volatility and labor market institutions, contributing to the understanding of how macroeconomic uncertainty and domestic labor market conditions shape international competitiveness.




with Hisahiro Naito
This paper evaluates whether satellite nighttime luminosity can serve as a proxy for household welfare in regions where traditional survey data are limited. Combining Demographic and Health Survey data with satellite nightlight observations, the study examines the potential of remote sensing indicators for monitoring socioeconomic development in low-data-capacity countries.




with Mohammad Abdul Malek and Kenichi Kashiwagi
This study investigates differences in agricultural productivity and resource-use efficiency among wheat-producing households in Afghanistan. Using household-level agricultural survey data and an endogeneity-corrected stochastic frontier model, the paper provides evidence on productivity constraints and policy-relevant factors affecting agricultural development in a conflict-affected and data-scarce setting.

Trade Hubs and the Uneven Gains from Globalization: Urban and Rural Disparities from Satellite Nighttime Lights Data
with Hisahiro Naito
This study examines whether the gains from export-driven globalization are distributed evenly across regions. The Effect of Exchange Rate Volatility and Labor Market Rigidity on Export Growth
with Hisahiro Naito
This paper investigates how exchange rate uncertainty interacts with labor market rigidity to influence export performance using country–industry panel data. Can DMSP Night Light Capture Household-Level Welfare? Evidence from a Cluster-Level Quasi-Panel of the Demographic and Health Survey
with Hisahiro Naito

Differential Farming Systems, Farm Productivity, and Resource Use Efficiency: The Case of Wheat Production in Afghanistan
with Mohammad Abdul Malek and Kenichi Kashiwagi
This research applies an endogeneity-corrected stochastic frontier model to household-level agricultural survey data to analyze productivity differences and resource-use efficiency among wheat-producing households in Afghanistan.

title: About
text:
About Me
I am Shafiqullah Yousafzai, a Ph.D. graduate in International Public Policy (Applied Economics) from the University of Tsukuba, Japan (2025).
My research interests lie at the intersection of international trade, development economics, spatial economics, economic geography, and applied econometrics. My research examines how globalization, trade integration, market access, and economic geography influence regional development, inequality, and household welfare.
My doctoral research focused on the economic consequences of exchange rate volatility, labor market conditions, exports, and regional inequality. I use quantitative methods combined with geospatial data, satellite nighttime lights, household surveys, and international trade datasets.
My current research projects include:

Trade hubs and regional inequality
International trade and household welfare
Trade integration and child labor
Agricultural productivity and technical efficiency
Market access and regional development
Transportation infrastructure and economic geography

I have experience with applied econometric methods and statistical software including Stata, R, QGIS, LaTeX, MATLAB, SPSS, and EViews.
This website provides information about my research, publications, teaching activities, and academic projects.

title: Research
text:
My research lies at the intersection of international trade, development economics, spatial economics, and economic geography. I study how globalization, market access, trade costs, and infrastructure influence regional development, inequality, and household welfare.




My research examines how international trade integration and market access affect regional economic outcomes, urban–rural inequality, and local development.
Key project:

Trade Hubs and the Uneven Gains from Globalization: Urban and Rural Disparities from Satellite Nighttime Lights Data

This project investigates whether locations connected to international trade networks experience different development outcomes compared with non-hub regions using satellite nighttime lights data and cross-country panel data.




I study how trade integration affects household welfare outcomes, including labor allocation, child labor, and health outcomes.
Key projects:

Trade Integration, Child Labor, and Rural–Urban Inequality in Sub-Saharan Africa
Trade and Infant Mortality: Evidence from Household Survey Data





My research also examines agricultural productivity, technical efficiency, and constraints faced by farmers in developing economies.
Key project:

Technical Efficiency of Wheat Production in Afghanistan

This research applies stochastic frontier analysis to investigate the determinants of agricultural productivity and efficiency.




I examine how transportation networks influence economic activity, connectivity, and regional development.
Current projects:

High-Speed Rail and Knowledge Spillovers
Road Quality and Trade Integration






My research uses applied econometric methods combined with spatial and geospatial data.
Methods: - Panel data econometrics - Instrumental variable estimation - Stochastic frontier analysis - Gravity models of trade - Spatial analysis
Data sources: - Satellite nighttime lights - Household surveys (DHS, ALCS) - International trade databases - Geographic information systems (GIS)
